newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ICTSI says volume surges in April, May.
newsitem.headline: ICTSI says volume surges in April, May.

text.p: Port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc (ICTSI) said on Monday traffic volume in its Manila port had picked up in April and May after a slow start in first quarter this year.
ICTSI president Rogelio Salazar told analysts at a briefing that volume reached more than 75,000 twenty foot equivalent units (TEUs) each in the months of April and May.
"In April alone, it was 45 percent higher than April of last year," Salazar said.
Comparative figures for May were not available.
In the first quarter, volume traffic rose only 2.7 percent to 204,529 TEU equivalent unts (TEUs).
Salazar said he expected the traffic to increase in the third and fourth quarter as international trade accelerates. ICTSI hit its record cargo handling of 79,000 TEU in August last year.
Chief financial officer Roberto Jayme said the 22 percent net income growth target remained achievable, despite a lower growth in the first three months of the year.
ICTSI reported a 43.9 million peso net income in the first quarter, down from 60.8 million in the same period last year.
The lower income was partly due to the one-time expense because of its downsizing programme.

Jayme said the laying off of 300 workers in March cost the company 15 million pesos. However, he estimated the savings from the laying off to reach four million pesos every month. The company currently employs 1,200 people.
ICTSI also said its inland container depot in Calamba town in the industrial Laguna province will be operational starting June 12 this year.
ICTSI will start decongesting its Manila port depot by transporting containers from the port to the depot twice every day, and eventually four trips a day.
The train will have 20 rail cars which can accommodate 40-foot container in each car.
The company will charge a transportation fee to cargo owners for the trips. The fee is expected to be lower than 3,300 per TEU being charged by local trucking service companies.
